title: Change and stability
note: Latin mutare, to change, gives mutable and immutable; Proteus, the shape-shifting sea god, gives protean. Decline has many shades: things wane and ebb gradually, atrophy from disuse, ossify into rigid habit, and fall into desuetude when no one uses them anymore.

items.a: liable to change
items.ex: Fashion is mutable; the human foot is not.

items.a: unchanging over time; unable to be changed
items.ex: The laws of physics are treated as immutable; tax law is not.

items.a: able to change form or take on many roles
d: rigid and set in its ways
items.ex: A protean actor, she played a queen, a thief and a talking dog in one season.

items.a: continuous change or flow
d: a return to an earlier state
items.ex: With the merger pending, every job title was in flux.

items.a: a complete change of form or nature
items.ex: The warehouse's metamorphosis into a concert hall took two years.

items.a: to change into another form or substance
items.ex: Alchemists hoped to transmute lead into gold.

items.a: to transform, often in a surprising or comic way
items.ex: The garage band's demo had been transmogrified into a soda jingle.

items.a: unwelcome changes of fortune
items.ex: The family business survived the vicissitudes of three recessions.

items.a: liable to change rapidly and unpredictably
items.ex: Crop prices were volatile all summer, swinging with every forecast.

items.a: to rise and fall irregularly
d: to break out again after a lull
items.ex: Her weight fluctuated by a few pounds with the seasons.

items.a: firmly set in a long-standing habit
items.ex: An inveterate gambler, he bet on which pigeon would fly first.

items.a: firmly established and hard to dislodge
items.ex: Entrenched interests blocked the reform for a decade.

items.a: to become rigid and resistant to change
items.ex: Without new members, the club's traditions ossified into empty ritual.

items.a: showing no activity or growth; not flowing
items.ex: Wages stayed stagnant while rents climbed.

items.a: near death; in terminal decline
items.ex: The moribund mill town found new life as an arts colony.

items.a: to waste away, especially from disuse
items.ex: Skills you never practice tend to atrophy.

items.a: to grow or expand rapidly
items.ex: Food trucks burgeoned downtown after the city eased its permit rules.

items.a: to decrease gradually in size, strength, or power
items.ex: Interest in the scandal waned once the hearings ended.

items.a: to flow back or recede, as a tide does
items.ex: As the tide ebbed, the old wreck rose out of the sand.

items.a: to become less intense or widespread
items.ex: The ferries waited for the storm to abate.

items.a: a new outbreak after a quiet period
items.ex: Officials feared a recrudescence of violence after the truce expired.

items.a: rising again after a decline
items.ex: The resurgent team won eight straight games after a dismal start.

items.a: lasting or recurring year after year
items.ex: Parking is the perennial complaint at every town meeting.

items.a: firm and unwavering in purpose or loyalty
items.ex: Through every lean season, her steadfast fans kept buying tickets.

items.a: a tendency to remain unchanged; resistance to change
d: a pattern of rising and falling
items.ex: Bureaucratic inertia kept the broken form in use for years.

items.a: in a state of inactivity or rest
items.ex: The volcano has been quiescent for a century, but not extinct.

items.a: rigid and unable to adapt
items.ex: Critics called the agency sclerotic, still filing paper forms in triplicate.

items.a: a state of disuse
items.ex: The old blue law had fallen into desuetude, though no one repealed it.

items.a: becoming outdated but still in use
items.ex: Fax machines were obsolescent long before offices threw them out.

items.a: a sudden, violent upheaval or disaster
d: a habit too old to break
items.ex: The war was a cataclysm that redrew the map of Europe.
